title: Rim-Schlessinger and finite tangent space give a versal formal object
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning that cartesian pullbacks exist along every base morphism and each fibre is a groupoid. A local ring has a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. Assume the Rim-Schlessinger property: whenever $B'=B\amalg_A A'$ is a pushout of spectra of Artinian local rings of finite type over $R$ and $A\to A'$ is a closed immersion defined by a nilpotent ideal, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal X(B')\simeq\mathcal X(B)\times_{\mathcal X(A)}\mathcal X(A')$. Fix a field $k$ of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $x_0\in\mathcal X(k)$. Assume the tangent space of deformations of $x_0$ is finite-dimensional over $k$: this is the vector space of isomorphism classes of objects over $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with an identified restriction $x_0$. A formal object over a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $(C,\mathfrak m)$ with residue field identified with $k$ is a system $\xi_n\in\mathcal X(C/\mathfrak m^n)$, $n\geq1$, with compatible transition isomorphisms; completeness means $C\cong\varprojlim_n C/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Such a system is versal if, for every surjection $B'\to B$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with residue field identified with $k$, every local $R$-map $C\to B$ inducing the identity on $k$, every $z\in\mathcal X(B')$, and every isomorphism $z|_B\cong\xi_B$ compatible with the specified identifications over $k$, there exist a local $R$-lift $C\to B'$ and an isomorphism $z\cong\xi_{B'}$ extending the prescribed isomorphism. Here $\xi_B$ denotes pullback from $\xi_n$ for any $n$ with $\mathfrak m^n$ mapping to zero in $B$, and similarly for $B'$. Then there exist such a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $(C,\mathfrak m)$ with residue field $k$ and a versal formal object $(\xi_n)$ with a specified isomorphism $\xi_1\cong x_0$. No effectivity or limit-preservation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07WU (lemma-deformation-category), remark-deformation-category-implies; Formal Deformation Theory, Tag 06IW (formal-defos.tex, lemma-versal-object-existence). This is their specialization to the deformation category of a fixed field-valued object.

proof.text: For $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$ define $\mathcal F(A)$ to consist of pairs $(x,\iota:x|_k\cong x_0)$, with arrows preserving $\iota$. Transport along a ring map is pullback in $\mathcal X$ along its spectrum map. The fibred-groupoid axioms provide the composition isomorphisms. Over $k$ the marked pair $(x_0,1)$ is terminal and every pair is uniquely isomorphic to it, so this is a predeformation category. For $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ with $A_2\to A$ surjective, the test-algebra lemma gives an Artinian local ring $P=A_1\times_A A_2$ with residue field $k$. Since $k$ is of finite type over $R$, the residue-field criterion makes $A_1$, $A_2$, $A$ and $P$ of finite type over $R$. Its spectrum is the scheme pushout by the affine pinching lemma. The kernel of $A_2\to A$ lies in the nilpotent maximal ideal, so the stated (RS) hypothesis applies. Passing from its equivalence to groupoids of objects with a chosen identification with $x_0$ preserves equivalence: an object and its marking lift by essential surjectivity, while a compatible arrow lifts uniquely by full faithfulness. Thus $\mathcal F$ satisfies (RS). This gives precisely the datum of the cited definition. In particular its tangent set is the given tangent space, with the same marking. The localization assertion in the test-algebra lemma permits use of the Stacks formal-deformation results even if $R\to k$ is not finite as a module map.

Put $d=\dim_kT\mathcal F$ and choose a basis $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d$. Choose algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $k$ over $R$; these exist by the finite type hypothesis. In the completed-polynomial lemma take $P=R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s,X_1,\ldots,X_d]$ with $Y_i\mapsto a_i$ and $X_i\mapsto0$, and denote its completion by $S$ and its maximal ideal by $\mathfrak m$. Let $W=k^d$ with basis $v_i$. Sending $Y_i$ to $(a_i,0)$ and $X_i$ to $(0,v_i)$ defines $P\twoheadrightarrow k[W]$. It extends to $S\twoheadrightarrow k[W]$ by the Artinian-map bijection in that lemma; surjectivity follows because the image already contains $k$ and all $v_i$. Put $J_1=\mathfrak m$ and let $J_2$ be its kernel, so $\mathfrak m^2\subseteq J_2\subseteq J_1$. Choose $\xi_1$ to be the marked object over $k$, and choose $\xi_2\in\mathcal F(S/J_2)$ with class $\sum_i\theta_i\otimes v_i$ under the tangent-tensor bijection. Its restriction has a unique isomorphism to $\xi_1$. The tangent-tensor lemma says that the induced maps $S/J_2\to k[\epsilon]$ realize every tangent class. The construction includes $d=0$, when $W=0$ and $J_2=J_1$.

source.place: Tag 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), Steps 1--2; polynomial completion in place of a formally smooth base followed by power series

proof.text: Inductively suppose $n\geq2$, $J_n\subseteq J_{n-1}$, $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq J_n$, and compatible marked objects through $\xi_n\in\mathcal F(S/J_n)$ have been chosen. Apply the least-liftable-ideal lemma to $B=S/(\mathfrak m J_n)\twoheadrightarrow S/J_n$ and $\xi_n$. This is an Artinian test algebra because $\mathfrak m^{n+1}\subseteq\mathfrak mJ_n$, and its kernel $J_n/(\mathfrak mJ_n)$ is killed by its maximal ideal. Let $J_{n+1}\subseteq S$ be the inverse image of the least liftable ideal. Then $\mathfrak mJ_n\subseteq J_{n+1}\subseteq J_n$, $\mathfrak m^{n+1}\subseteq J_{n+1}$, and there is $\xi_{n+1}\in\mathcal F(S/J_{n+1})$ with a chosen isomorphism restricting it to $\xi_n$. Choose these successively. Crucially, for every ideal $K$ with $\mathfrak mJ_n\subseteq K\subseteq J_n$ admitting a lift of $\xi_n$, leastness gives $J_{n+1}\subseteq K$. This records both the inductive invariant and the universal property needed below.

Set $J=\bigcap_{n\geq1}J_n$ and $C=S/J$. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$, this is a proper quotient. The complete-local-quotient lemma makes $C$ Noetherian complete local with residue field $k$. The descending-ideal lemma applies because $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq J_n$ and identifies $(J_n/J)$ with a cofinal filtration for its maximal-ideal topology. The formal-filtration comparison sends the compatible system $(\xi_n)$ to a formal object $\xi$ on $C$, compatibly identifying its value at $S/J_n$ with $\xi_n$. In particular its first residue object is $x_0$ with its marking. Every tangent map from $S/J_2$ obtained in step 2 factors through $C$, because $J\subseteq J_2$. Its value under $\xi$ is the value of $\xi_2$, by the evaluation clause of the comparison. Consequently the tangent map for $\xi$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), passage to the quotient and the first versality condition

proof.text: To check the remaining condition of the tangent-ring-lift criterion, take a small extension $B\twoheadrightarrow A$, a local $a:C\to A$, an object $y\in\mathcal F(B)$ and the prescribed isomorphism $y|_A\cong\xi_A$. The maximal ideal of $A$ is nilpotent by the test-algebra lemma; hence $a$ kills some power of the maximal ideal of $C$. Cofinality in step 4 gives $n\geq2$ such that $a$ factors through $S/J_n\to A$. The evaluation clause of the filtration comparison identifies $\xi_A$ with the restriction of $\xi_n$, including the chosen arrow to $A$. Form $B_n=(S/J_n)\times_A B$. It is a test algebra and $p:B_n\to S/J_n$ is a small extension by the test-algebra lemma. The (RS) equivalence for $\mathcal F$ lifts the triple consisting of $\xi_n$, $y$, and the prescribed isomorphism to an object over $B_n$ restricting to $\xi_n$. If $p$ has a section $t$, the composite $C\to S/J_n\xrightarrow{t}B_n\to B$ already lifts $a$. It remains to handle the case without a section.

source.place: Tag 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), versality proof up to the section case

proof.text: In the nonsplit case the essential-surjection lemma applies to $p:B_n\to S/J_n$. The completed-polynomial lifting property lifts $S\to S/J_n\to A$ to $h:S\to B$. Together with the quotient map $S\twoheadrightarrow S/J_n$ this defines $g:S\to B_n$, $s\mapsto(s\bmod J_n,h(s))$. It is local and induces the identity on $k$. Its composite with $p$ is surjective, so the complete-source clause of the essential-surjection lemma makes $g$ surjective. Put $K=\ker(g)$. Since $p\circ g$ is the quotient map, $K\subseteq J_n$. Since $g(J_n)\subseteq\ker(p)$ and that kernel is killed by the maximal ideal of $B_n$, locality gives $g(\mathfrak mJ_n)=0$, hence $\mathfrak mJ_n\subseteq K$. Under $S/K\cong B_n$, the object supplied in step 5 is a lift of $\xi_n$ to $S/K$. Step 3 therefore gives $J_{n+1}\subseteq K$. Thus $g$ factors through $S/J_{n+1}$, and projecting to $B$ gives a lift $S/J_{n+1}\to B$ of $S/J_{n+1}\to S/J_n\to A$. Precomposing with $C\to S/J_{n+1}$ gives the required local lift $C\to B$.

Steps 5--6 establish the underlying-ring lifting condition for every small extension and every prescribed deformation comparison. Step 4 established tangent surjectivity. The tangent-ring-lift criterion now supplies the object isomorphism extending that prescribed comparison and gives versality for every Artinian surjection. Forget the markings in the resulting formal system to obtain objects in $\mathcal X(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$; its retained residue marking gives $\xi_1\cong x_0$. Versality in $\mathcal X$ follows from versality in $\mathcal F$: given a surjection $B'\to B$, a local $C\to B$, $z\in\mathcal X(B')$ and $\beta:z|_B\cong\xi_B$, mark $z$ by the composite $z|_k\cong(z|_B)|_k\cong\xi_B|_k\cong x_0$ obtained from $\beta$ and the marking of $\xi$. Then $\beta$ is an arrow of $\mathcal F(B)$. Versality in $\mathcal F$ gives a local lift $C\to B'$ and a marked arrow $z\cong\xi_{B'}$ restricting to $\beta$, which is in particular an isomorphism in $\mathcal X(B')$. This is exactly the claimed formal versal object. All operations took place on Artinian quotients and compatible formal systems; none required an effective object over $C$ or preservation of limits.
